messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

output:
Drafted below. I don't know your team's actual specifics, so the numbers, names, and months are in brackets — swap them and it's ready to post.

---

**What we actually did this year**

Twelve months ago a deploy took [40 minutes] and our bug tracker was a place tickets went to die. Both of those are gone.

The first half of the year went to the migration. [Priya] mapped the dependency graph in January, we found the three services everyone had quietly forked, and we spent until [May] untangling them. Boring work. It also took p99 from [1.4s to 310ms], which is the only reason anyone outside the team noticed.

Then the on-call rewrite. We deleted [62] alerts and kept [11], and paging dropped from about [nine a week] to [two]. Worth being honest: we got this wrong twice first. The initial pass cut alerts we turned out to need, and [October] was miserable because of it.

Things we said we'd do and didn't — the flaky-test project, the docs rewrite, moving off [RabbitMQ]. The queue is [next year's] problem. I'd rather write that here than bury it in a roadmap slide where it quietly rolls forward for another twelve months.

What sticks with me is how much of this year's value came from subtraction. [17,000] lines removed net, two services retired, one database gone. Nobody gets promoted for that, which is a thing we should probably fix.

For [2027] the shortlist is short on purpose: [the queue migration], [the read-path cache], and whatever the on-call rotation tells us is still broken. Everything else waits.

---

~250 words. Tell me the real numbers and I'll fill them in.
